title: Never paid royalties on his 1959 records
summary: Lewis got $400 for his 1959 record but no royalties, and Allen suggests finding a lawyer.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: So many of them died that way. So many musicians never got a break. That's the truth. And Shade made some records and everything himself. Yeah he did. You think he'd have made a little money out of that and got something coming in.
Oh yeah, well did he. Well I made records and signed a contract and everything. I was supposed to get so much and so much on the record and nearly get a penny.
They didn't pay you when they made them?
Well you know they give you something but you know I'm talking about you're supposed to get so much off a record.
Yeah I know what you mean.

Well yeah, nearly get a penny off that. But I got $400 but yet and still that, they were supposed to give me that after I made the record but yet and still I was supposed to get a royale. There was so much and so much on each record was sold. And that was in 59. And I ain't get a nickel yet.
Well that's what you expect man. I tell you. That's what he did. That's the way they do all the time.
That's why my wife would tell you the same thing. I need to get a nickel out of it. No more than that what the people got through making the record like that.
